answer: At the Grand Canyon, two pounds of fluorescein poured into a wash reappeared kilometres away glowing above 0.01 parts per billion. A ballot is the same: like a comet it streaks through a karst conduit, releasing its dye at its spring, as verifiers shine a lantern to catch the glow. A farm minting 10,000 ballots from one spring dies by the dilution check: one spring's dye split 10,000 ways falls below 0.01 ppb after weeks of sampling, the lantern finds nothing, every ballot fails the glow test and forfeits its $25 bond — $250,000 gone. One comet, one spring; a shared plume glows too faint.
